title: Negation
concept: The minus sign - can negate a value, flipping its sign from positive to negative or vice versa.
why: Negation lets you express opposites — loss instead of gain, below zero instead of above, reverse direction.
syntax_ref:
-value     → negation (unary minus)
a - b       → subtraction (binary minus)
tips: `-` before a value negates it; `-` between values subtracts
Negating a negative makes it positive: `-(-5)` = `5`
Negation works on both Int and Float64
Use parentheses to be clear: `-(a + b)` vs `-a + b`
common_mistakes: Confusing `-x` (negation) with `0 - x` — they give the same result but mean different things
Forgetting parentheses: `-a + b` means `(-a) + b`, not `-(a + b)`
Thinking `--x` is valid XIOM — use `-(-x)` or just `x`
